quotes.text: Intune is not the fortress. It is the field instrument that measures health, applies posture, and signals the identity gate when a device is trustworthy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Intune's role in Zero Trust in one clear image.

quotes.text: Everything else earns access, document every exclusion with an owner, a reason and an expiry. Review monthly. If you remember nothing else remember this. Exclusions expand over time unless they are pruned.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete governance rule for Conditional Access exclusions.

quotes.text: The thing most people miss is that temporary exceptions become permanent features unless they're tracked. If you remember nothing else, remember this. Defaults first, exceptions last, documentation always.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable principle for keeping security baselines from drifting.

quotes.text: Privilege identity management places roles in an eligible state. Administrators activate when needed prove themselves with MFA, explain their reason, request approval where appropriate and accept a time bound window.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Describes what a healthy just-in-time admin model looks like.

quotes.text: without rings every change is a bet on perfection. A single mis-scoped assignment can deny access to mail, break VPN clients or collide with older profiles.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

Field audit in the admin center and PowerShell

takeaways: Intune only measures device health; it protects the tenant when compliance, Conditional Access and privileged access work together, so build layered CA policies in report-only mode first and keep exclusions surgical, owned and expiring.

Adopt Microsoft's security baselines for Windows, Defender and Edge, align compliance policies to them and convert standing admin roles to eligible PIM assignments with MFA, justification and compliant-device activation.

Protect BYOD with app protection policies and approved client apps, block legacy authentication, and roll out every change through pilot, early adopter and broad rings backed by a weekly Graph or PowerShell audit.
hook: A green Intune dashboard can still hide weak Conditional Access, drifting baselines, standing admin rights, unmanaged BYOD and reckless rollouts. This episode is for endpoint and identity admins who want to know why their Intune deployment may be a security risk. Learn the five misconfigurations attackers exploit and the concrete fixes and audits you can run in the admin center, Graph and PowerShell.
